stories.title: $ANSEM Memecoin Drops 90% from Summer Peak, Splitting Community
stories.hook: Ansem's Black Bull memecoin rocketed to $0.44 in July, but now sits at just $0.03—leaving holders cheering a bargain and critics crying foul.
stories.summary: Launched in mid-June 2026 on Solana's Pump.fun, $ANSEM surged after influencer Ansem received a big supply share, ran million-dollar airdrops, and boosted its market cap into hundreds of millions. It peaked early July before plunging over 90%, now trading around $0.033 with a $14 million circulating cap. Critics accuse Ansem of holding over 50% and selling via side wallets, while supporters call it oversold, a 'generational entry,' and stick by his 'not a loss until you sell' stance amid ongoing games and rewards. The divide highlights memecoin volatility, with early winners and late losers watching for the next move.

stories.title: $USELESS Promoter Calls Dip a Buying Opportunity
stories.hook: Unipcs, the voice behind $USELESS memecoin, sees the latest price plunge not as trouble, but as a prime chance to buy in.
stories.summary: The Solana-based $USELESS token, launched in May 2025 as a satirical take on utility-free coins, has dropped 12% in the past day to around $0.077, with a $77 million market cap—down 82% from its October 2025 peak of $0.43. Unipcs shared that this sharp correction among memecoins is 'not a bug. It’s a feature,' highlighting how the coin swings big in both bull and bear markets, creating entry points for potential cycle leaders. Community responses mix support with skepticism over timing and performance, while Unipcs discloses his 3% supply holding and insists past rallies came from organic interest.

stories.title: $ANSEM Memecoin Crashes 90% from Peak Amid Community Split
stories.hook: One holder watched unrealized gains near $1.5 million vanish, selling for just $25,000 and telling family retirement dreams were over. 'It’s honestly heartbreaking,' they shared.
stories.summary: The Solana memecoin $ANSEM, tied to influencer Ansem (@blknoiz06), launched anonymously in mid-June 2026 and rocketed to a $400 million market cap with prices near $0.44 in July. By late November, it plunged over 90% to $0.033 and a $33 million cap, fueled by large sell orders like swaps of 100,000 tokens for $7,800-$8,000 in stablecoins. Ansem posted a grim chart calling it a 'shitcoin chart,' splitting fans—some accuse him of shilling while others see a buying opportunity, with his wallet still holding a big share.

stories.title: Traders Debate Memecoins' Future Amid Market Cooldown
stories.hook: With Bitcoin hovering near $62,000 after recent drops, traders are split on whether memecoins can rebound like old favorites Doge and Pepe.
stories.summary: The memecoin sector's $20.5 billion market has fallen sharply, as daily launches on Solana mostly fail—only 0.14 percent survive with decent liquidity and volume. Some traders argue quality community projects will deliver huge gains, while others doubt billion-dollar runs will return, blaming the flood of low-quality tokens. Defenders point to memecoins' history before NFTs and predict one big winner could quiet the skeptics, with memes like 'big pump soon' rockets fueling the ongoing optimism.

stories.title: Solana Co-Founder Asks About Mustache Cat Memecoin
stories.hook: Anatoly Yakovenko, Solana's co-founder, posted a simple question on November 18: 'What’s up with the mustache cat? Good or bad?' It opened the floodgates to a wave of cat memes and lively debate.
stories.summary: The 'mustache cat,' or Ni Hao Cat, powers $MIHAO, a Solana memecoin launched on Pump.fun on October 25, featuring an orange tabby with a long white mustache inspired by the Chinese greeting 'ni hao.' It gained buzz after trader Ansem set it as his profile picture in mid-November, leading to a market cap peak above $20 million before settling near $6.7 million as of November 20. Fans shared creative edits of the cat in samurai armor or beach scenes, calling it a true community coin, while skeptics wondered about coordinated hype and volatility. Yakovenko's query highlighted Solana's playful meme culture amid optimism and caution.

stories.title: Traders Question Memecoin Days and Perps Potential
stories.hook: Crypto traders are looking back at memecoin booms that once hit $88.8 billion peaks, now wondering if steady wins await through perps trading alone.
stories.summary: Discussions highlight how the biggest 2021 memecoin reached $88.8 billion while 2026's top one sits at $897 million, signaling the hype era may be over. Platforms like Pump.fun and Fomo now draw focus for perps trading, with users debating if discipline in futures can replace meme riches without scams. Success stories remain scarce, as most big wins tied to memes, though some see less competition for skilled traders amid cooling volumes and rising fatigue with quick flips.

stories.title: Memecoin Traders Voice Frustration Over Hype-Driven Market
stories.hook: Traders in the memecoin world are tired of prices swinging on nothing but hype and a few big-name shouts, leaving real trading skill in the dust.
stories.summary: In the memecoin space, especially on Solana's Pump.fun platform, participants complain that tokens live or die by quick hype from known voices rather than any solid metrics like earnings. One trader called it 'wallet capital markets,' where short-lived pumps dominate and chart-watchers sell fastest without those boosts. While some stay selective amid low liquidity and advise waiting for better conditions, others hold out hope for billion-dollar coins to return as activity cools and Pump.fun's own token dips below past highs.

stories.title: Crypto Traders Challenge Each Other to Pick Next $100M Memecoin
stories.hook: One trader posted a dramatic 'gun to your head' challenge: name a memecoin hitting $100 million market cap by next year, or else.
stories.summary: Traders are ramping up the hunt for memecoins that could explode, with the sector's total market cap hovering between $19.9 billion and $22.7 billion despite recent price dips. Enthusiasts highlight how these tokens can turn zeros into millions overnight through pure buyer momentum, no earnings needed, as one noted the space once hit $50 billion on narrative alone. Skeptics mention fading retail buzz and losses, but daily shill requests and bold bets keep the high-stakes conversation alive.

stories.title: Summer 2026 Memecoins Plunge 80-99% from Peaks
stories.hook: Tokens like DOPE, SC, and FATCOIN that lit up summer trading now sit 98% below highs, leaving traders to debate quick flips or total wipeouts.
stories.summary: Charts shared widely show dozens of popular memecoins down over 98% from all-time highs, with half of 365 notable ones from the last cycle falling at least 99.8%. Traders mix caution and opportunism: some warn against long-term holds since most head to zero, others eye buy-ins amid the selloff or stick to established assets like ETH. The overall memecoin market cap has contracted sharply alongside broader crypto weakness, fueling talks of short-term trades versus patient 'hold culture' for potential rebounds.

stories.title: Trader Shares $193K Loss on Artificial Inu After $10M Peak Gains
stories.hook: A fomo app trader posted a stark screenshot of a 71.4% drop on Artificial Inu, down $193,426, with a cryptic note: 'One day I’ll tell the full story. Today is not that day.'
stories.summary: The screenshot highlighted the red drawdown next to the token’s cat mascot in a blue hoodie, prompting replies that recalled the trader's earlier $10 million unrealized gains. Community members questioned holding through the peak, with some joking 'you made $10M WTF more do you even want,' while others speculated on side wallets or team ties. Artificial Inu trades on Robinhood Chain against tokenized Nvidia stock, known for wild swings from its September peak above $0.38 to now near $0.0216. The post highlights memecoin trading's classic risks, where big runs tempt holders but reversals wipe out profits fast.
